# Orbit Store for PS4 (Beta)

> A modern PS4 download manager with resumable downloads, a native TV app, browser controls, phone pairing and the Orbit Zero desktop companion.

The official project is https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4. The PS5 version is at https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5. Orbit Store has no official social media accounts. It is free to use, and nothing is locked behind a payment. Optional contributions help cover the costs of AI tools, test consoles, hardware and servers. Optional crypto support is available through the addresses at https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/issues/131#user-content-support-with-crypto.

The current PS4 release is Orbit Store 0.2.0 (beta): native TV app 0.2.0 (orbit_store_ps4.pkg) with download service 0.2.0 (orbit_store.elf), plus Orbit Zero 1.9.7. It was tested on a PS4 on firmware 12.00 with GoldHEN; 0.0.3 added support for firmware 13.52 and 14.00, not yet tested on a console. 0.2.0 adds Free up space: when a game doesn't fit on its drive, Download opens Not enough space, which lists what Orbit could delete from that drive, biggest first: its own leftovers (packages the PS4 has already installed, archives kept after unpacking and cancelled downloads), ticked for you, and the games installed on that drive, for you to choose. Orbit deletes what you pick one at a time, uninstalling a ticked game as from the PS4 home screen, then starts the download. Saves are not touched, and a game whose package Orbit kept can be installed again from Downloads. USB drives list no games; homebrew apps and Orbit itself are never listed. Free up space is also in Library and on a download paused for room to unpack. 0.2.0 also downloads files from your own direct links: in Downloads, Download from links takes up to 20 https links, and Replace link continues a download whose link expired, keeping the part already downloaded. Browse can sort by Recently added. When TorBox's download server can't be reached, Orbit asks TorBox for a fresh link up to 3 times before suggesting another CDN. Orbit follows Vikingfile's move of its file pages to a new address (vik1ngf1le.online). Catalogue revision 101 adds 5 PS4 games (Embr, GigaBash, Jitsu Squad, Slay the Princess - The Pristine Cut and Spirit of the North), for 1,739 in all. 0.1.0 added Get everything: on a game's page, Orbit lists the game, the newest update the PS4's firmware can run and the game's DLC, adds them to Downloads in one go and installs them in order (game, update, DLC). It also added game updates: Library shows each installed game's version and marks games with a newer update (410 PS4 games have updates, including backports for older firmware); Update or Update all in Library's Updates downloads and installs them by themselves. 0.1.0 can keep ZIP, 7z and RAR downloads packed (turn off Extract archives after downloading in App settings → Storage & cleanup), unpacks RAR with RARLAB's UnRAR on several CPU cores, needs room only for the archive when a download is added and checks for room to unpack just before unpacking. It keeps downloaded covers across restarts, fixes TorBox waits and resubmits, no longer closes when the PS4's network drops, brings the TV app back after a Vikingfile or AkiraBox page and added 300 PS4 games. 0.0.3 added Stream & install from Orbit Zero, Metacritic scores and HowLongToBeat playtimes (now 543 and 932 PS4 games) with Browse filters and sorting, a remembered Direct/TorBox choice with an optional Always use TorBox setting, and no limit on the number of installs. Orbit Zero 1.9.1 or later, the companion app for Mac, Windows and Linux, works with a PS4 running Orbit Store 0.0.2 or later: it downloads games on the computer and sends them to the PS4 to install, opens Vikingfile and AkiraBox pages on the computer so their Cloudflare check passes in seconds, and starts Orbit on the PS4 (sending elfldr through GoldHEN's payload loader first when no ELF loader runs). With Download preference set to Prefer PS4, Zero hands the link it caught to the PS4, which downloads the game itself. Zero keeps one profile per console and uses one console at a time. Guide: https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/blob/main/guides/orbit-zero.md

## Catalogue

The PS4 catalogue lists 1,739 PS4 games with 1,856 single-file download options from Archive.org, Vikingfile and AkiraBox, plus 564 add-ons with 566 options across 125 base games. There is no platform filter; every entry is a PS4 (CUSA) title. Formats are PKG and FPKG packages, either raw or inside a single ZIP, RAR or 7z archive. Multipart archives are not supported. Sources are opt-in.

Discover opens first. Store shows New on Orbit, Latest releases and an All games grid; Crossbar, Cinema and Panorama arrange these collections differently. Browse supports source, format, genre, tag, region and download-size filters, search, sorting, Installed games and shared favourites. Filter choices show matching game counts. Genre allows several selections; only genres recorded for at least ten games appear. Tags are PlayStation exclusive, Local co-op, Split-screen, Open world, Story-driven, Soulslike, Turn-based and PSVR supported. In the TV app, Square toggles favourites in Store; Triangle does so in Crossbar, Cinema and Panorama.

New games and corrections arrive through catalogue updates. Orbit checks when it starts and every six hours; App settings → Game catalogue → Refresh catalogue checks manually. If a refresh fails with HTTP 0 or a network error, the saved catalogue stays usable. Queued downloads keep the file originally chosen.

## Install and use Orbit Store

Orbit needs a PS4 with GoldHEN. Turn on GoldHEN's payload loader once (GoldHEN → Servers Settings → Enable PayLoader Server). Close other apps, such as ezRemote, before opening Orbit; programs started this way share memory with open apps.

- TV app: install orbit_store_ps4.pkg with GoldHEN's Package Installer (Settings → Debug Settings → Package Installer). Orbit Store appears on the Games row. The package includes the download service and elfldr, an ELF loader. Nothing has to run first: the app gives elfldr to GoldHEN's payload loader and starts the service through it. Right after the PS4 turns on, the first start can take up to about 40 seconds longer. The TV app's title ID is ORBT00002.
- Browser version: send orbit_store.elf once to an ELF loader on port 9021, such as elfldr. GoldHEN's own payload loader (port 9090) and LaunchPad cannot run the full ELF; it is too big. Orbit saves its service and elfldr in /data/orbit-store/ and adds the Orbit Store Browser icon (ORBT00001), which opens http://127.0.0.1:34177/ in the PS4's Internet Browser while Orbit is running. The icon cannot start a stopped service.
- Phone or computer: open http://<ps4-ip>:34177/ on the same local network and pair with the six-digit code shown on the PS4.

Auto-start is opt-in. App settings → Updates & startup → Payload managers → Add Orbit places a small starter in GoldHEN LaunchPad (/data/payloads) or Homebrew Launcher and keeps it current. GoldHEN AutoRun (GoldHEN 2.4b18.10 or newer) can then run that starter when GoldHEN loads; Orbit edits only its own entries in /data/GoldHEN/payloads.ini. The starter sends the saved service to elfldr, starting elfldr through GoldHEN's payload loader first when needed.

Update Orbit is under App settings → Updates & startup (Settings → Updates & startup in other layouts). It updates the TV app and service together; select Close and reopen afterward. Reopening saves the queue, stops the older service and starts the new one, resuming interrupted downloads. Restart Orbit restarts only the service. Loading an ELF while Orbit runs saves it for the next start. The update panel shows Running, Saved for next start and Latest release separately. Your settings and queue are in /data/orbit-store/.

## Downloads

Open a game's Download options to choose Source, Download using (direct or TorBox) and Save to (a PS4 drive). Direct options start with Download to PS4. Vikingfile first asks for the file with the signed-in session; if verification is needed, its page opens full screen on the PS4: complete verification, move the pointer to Download with the left stick and press ○. AkiraBox: select Open AkiraBox on PS4 (TV app) or Open download page on PS4 (browser), complete verification, then select Download; an ad may appear instead, so close it and try again or choose another source. Orbit catches the ready link, checks it against the chosen file and returns to the app. Provider pages appear on the PS4 even when started from a phone.

Downloads go to the selected drive's homebrew folder: /data/homebrew/ for internal storage, /mnt/usbN/homebrew/ for USB drives. Connections per download: 1–64, default 8, with 64 shared across active downloads; TorBox uses at most eight per game. Simultaneous downloads: 1–8, default 1. Download recovery: automatic retries 0–10 (default 3), 10 seconds between retries, reconnect below 1 KiB/s for 60 seconds. Downloads keep running when the TV app or browser is closed; Orbit does not download in rest mode.

ZIP, RAR and 7z downloads unpack on the selected PS4 drive. Known passwords are tried automatically: DLPSGAME.COM, [DLPSGAME.COM], SuperPSX, www.DLPSGAME.COM, downloadgameps3.com, hako and pippo. Otherwise use Enter archive password, then Retry extraction. Delete archives after extracting is on by default. From 0.1.0, a ZIP, RAR or 7z download needs room only for itself when added; Orbit checks for room for its files just before unpacking and, without it, pauses the download with the archive kept until space is freed and Resume is selected. Extract archives after downloading (on by default) can be turned off to keep archives packed.

Optional accounts: Archive.org (email and password sent once; only the sign-in is kept, never the password), Vikingfile (account hash entered on Vikingfile's official page; the TV app and browser keep separate sessions) and TorBox (API key, connected once in the browser and shared). Notifications can go to the PS4, to ntfy, or both. Automatic PS4 shutdown is off by default and shows a 60-second countdown you can cancel once downloads, installations and file operations finish.

## Installing, Library and Files

Install on PS4 hands a finished PKG or FPKG to the PS4's own package installer (BGFT). A plain download never installs automatically; Get everything and Library updates (0.1.0) install by themselves, in order. The PS4 chooses its installation storage. Downloaded packages are kept unless App settings → Storage & cleanup → Installed packages → Delete packages after installing is on (off by default). Check installation recovers an unconfirmed result; Orbit never resubmits an uncertain installation by itself or uninstalls a game. Game images (exFAT, FFPFSC, FFPKG) and game folders are PS5 ShadowMount formats and are not supported on PS4.

Library lists the games installed on the PS4, read from the console's own app folders; no ShadowMount is needed. It refreshes automatically. Library cannot mount, copy, move or start games; from 0.2.0 it uninstalls a game only when the user ticks it in Free up space. Library → Files browses internal storage and USB drives: open folders, copy, move, rename, delete, measure, unpack ZIP/RAR/7z and install PKG/FPKG files. A paired phone or computer can save a file with Save to this device.

## Interfaces, settings and languages

Store is the default interface; Crossbar, Cinema and Panorama are also available in the TV app and browser. Select Keep within 15 seconds to save a choice. All offer Full or Reduced motion; Crossbar has time-of-day ribbons, Cinema blurred art or plain black behind menus, and Panorama four accent colours and faint art or plain black behind pages. Settings categories: Downloads, Storage & cleanup, Sources & accounts, Devices, Appearance, Notifications, Game catalogue, Updates & startup, Diagnostics & about and Support Orbit (App settings in Store, Settings elsewhere).

Orbit supports 26 interface languages: English, Arabic, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian Bokmål, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Portuguese (Portugal), Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Ukrainian, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. Arabic mirrors the layout.

## Orbit Zero

Orbit Zero 1.9.7 is the companion app for Mac, Windows and Linux (Orbit-Zero-1.9.7-* packages on the PS4 release, checked with SHA256SUMS). It works with a PS4 running Orbit Store 0.0.2 or later (Get everything and game updates in Zero need Orbit Store 0.1.0 or later; Free up space, Download from links and Replace link in Zero need Orbit Store 0.2.0), over Wi-Fi or Ethernet on the same home network; the PS4 doesn't need internet for computer downloads. Settings → Updates & startup → PS4 → Start Orbit on PS4 gets Orbit for PS4 from GitHub on the computer and sends it to the ELF loader on port 9021, starting Zero's included elfldr through GoldHEN's payload loader (port 9090) first if needed. Pair with Settings → Devices → Show code on PS4, then Pair with PS4.

With a PS4 paired, Browse and Add-ons list PS4 games and add-ons only. Downloads show Download to computer, Extract on computer (ZIP, RAR and 7z) and Transfer to PS4; Install on PS4 installs a transferred package. Save to → This computer keeps a game on the computer; Send to PS4 transfers it later. Vikingfile and AkiraBox pages open on the computer, where their Cloudflare check usually passes in seconds. Settings → Downloads → Download preference: Computer (default) downloads on the computer and sends the files; Prefer PS4 lets the PS4 download directly, and for Vikingfile and AkiraBox hands the caught link to the PS4. With Orbit Store 0.0.3 or later, Stream & install installs a finished computer download straight from the computer without a copy on the PS4; packages the PS4 can't install that way get a message to send them to the PS4 instead. Zero 1.9.2's included elfldr supports firmware 13.52 and 14.00; with Zero 1.9.1 on those firmware versions, Start Orbit on PS4 needs an ELF loader already running. Library, Files, saved filters and automatic PS4 shutdown work with the paired PS4. In the TV app, App settings → Devices → Enable Orbit Zero sends downloads started on the PS4 through Zero. One Orbit Zero can keep a PS5 and a PS4 as separate profiles, one connected at a time. Zero keeps its own Archive.org, Vikingfile and TorBox sign-ins on the computer; TorBox in Zero uses at most four connections per game. Its optional local API for other apps is under Settings → Devices → Connected apps.

## Downloads

- [Current release](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/releases/latest): Version, changes, installation steps, source bundle and checksums.
- [Native TV app](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/releases/latest/download/orbit_store_ps4.pkg): The Games-row app, including the Orbit service and elfldr.
- [TV app SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/releases/latest/download/orbit_store_ps4.pkg.sha256): Verify the PKG before installing.
- [Current ELF](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/releases/latest/download/orbit_store.elf): The download service and browser interface.
- [ELF SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/releases/latest/download/orbit_store.elf.sha256): Verify the ELF before loading it.
- Orbit Zero for Mac, Windows and Linux: the Orbit-Zero-* packages and SHA256SUMS on the [current release](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/releases/latest).
- [Payload feed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/main/payloads.json): Orbit's ELF URL, version and checksum for payload managers that support custom sources.

## Support

- [Issues](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps4/issues): Report problems with the Orbit version, PS4 firmware, GoldHEN version and steps to reproduce. Keep pairing codes and private information out of reports.
